issues.title: parser: splitLine drops the last field of a line that ends with a comma
issues.body: `splitLine` in `src/parser/split.ts` drops the last field of a line that ends with a comma: `a,b,` gives two fields, not three. Done when `splitLine` keeps that empty last field.

issues.title: An imported table has one column less than its file
issues.body: I imported a CSV file, and the table has one column less than the file has.

comments.author: kim
comments.body: Same cause as #91: `importTable` splits each line with `splitLine`, which drops the empty last field. Reproduced: the line `x,1,` under the header `name,price,note` gives the row `["x","1"]`. The fix for #91 guards `importTable` too.

issues.title: parser: splitLine cuts a quoted field that holds a comma
issues.body:
Where: `src/parser/split.ts:4`, `splitLine`.

How it shows up: `splitLine('"Smith, J",5')` gives `["\"Smith", " J\"", "5"]`, not `["Smith, J", "5"]`. The row gets one column more than the header, and the quotes stay in the data. `importTable` uses `splitLine`, so an imported table shows it too.

Why out of scope: found in the review of #91. That fix only keeps an empty last field. Quoted fields need a real field scanner, which is larger than that fix.

issues.title: importTable keeps a carriage return at the end of each line of a CRLF file
issues.body:
Where: `src/import-table.ts:5`, `importTable` splits the text on `\n` only.

How it shows up: `importTable("name,price,note\r\nx,1,\r\n")` gives `[["name","price","note\r"],["x","1","\r"],[""]]`. The last cell of each row keeps `\r`, so a file saved on Windows gives a header `note\r`, and an empty last cell is `\r`, not empty.

Why out of scope: found in the review of #91, which changes only `src/parser/split.ts`.

issues.title: parser: parseRows and splitLine split a line in two different ways
issues.body:
Where: `src/parser/read.ts:60` (`parseRows` splits on comma or tab and unquotes) and `src/parser/split.ts:4` (`splitLine` splits on comma only, used by `importTable`).

How it shows up: for `a\tb,`, `parseRows` gives `["a","b",""]`, and `importTable` gives `["a\tb",""]`. The two paths can drift apart each time one of them changes.

Why out of scope: found in the review of #91. Which splitter stays is a design choice.

issues.title: importTable gives a row for an empty line, as the one after the last newline
issues.body:
Where: `src/import-table.ts:5`.

How it shows up: `importTable("name,price\nx,1\n")` gives a last row `[""]` for the empty text after the last newline. Before #91 it gave `[]`. Both are a row that the file does not hold as data.

Question: must `importTable` skip empty lines, or only the empty text after the last newline? The docs and the tests do not say.

Why out of scope: found in the review of #91. That fix makes `splitLine` give one empty field for an empty line, as for any other line with no comma. What the table does with empty lines is a product rule.
